mentl/45d7439:
Two fixes, one discipline — lower reads what the graph/infer already
encoded, instead of dereferencing or punishing what it doesn't know.

1. NFre gradient resolution (lookup.wat). $lookup_ty's NFree arm no
   longer treats a free type variable as a compiler-internal error. Under
   uniform-i32 (SUBSTRATE.md §IX) representation is invariant under type:
   a value whose type is open flows as a uniform i32 regardless. So NFree
   returns TVar(handle) — the honest type — not an E_UnresolvedType +
   sentinel. This resolves spec 05 invariant 2's last monomorphization-era
   binary toward the gradient (ULTIMATE_MEDIUM.md §9.3). The genuinely
   type-load-bearing consumer (classify_handler's TCont guard) keeps its
   own guard; the four value-position consumers already flow a
   non-concrete type as uniform i32. NErrorHole stays the error path.

2. Expr-tag sentinel read (walk_call.wat). $lower_expr read the Expr tag
   via a raw (i32.load offset=0) on the variant — dereferencing a
   nullary-sentinel variant (LitUnit=84 and kin) into the sentinel region
   [0,4096) → tag 0 → the unknown-tag catch-all → LConst(0) corruption.
   Now reads via $tag_of, exactly as infer's $walk_expr_expr_tag does:
   sentinel < heap_base IS the tag; only heap records are dereferenced.
   The SAME-reader discipline — lower classifies the Expr the way infer
   classified it.

Measured: wheel "E_UnresolvedType" (misnamed; mostly unknown-tag) 3854 →
76 (98%). Regression battery (10 micro-tests) all rc=0 / 0 diagnostics /
valid WAT. Trace-harness suite 66/17 unchanged (the 17 are pre-existing).
mentl2.wat validates. The remaining mentl2 first-light trap is a distinct
(unreachable) mid handler-chain-install in compile_stdin — named next.

mentl/454d27a:
Implements effect subtraction operator for the effect algebra. Syntax `with E - F`
now desugars to `with E, !F` (present E, remove F), providing an intuitive alternative
to negation constraints that reads as "capability removal."

Also fixes: builtin/operation name collision across modules. When a custom effect
operation shadows a builtin function (e.g., custom `log(String)` vs builtin
`log(Float)`), the checker now correctly disambiguates based on the function's
declared effects. Functions declaring an effect dispatch to that effect operation;
functions not declaring it resolve to builtins. This enables correct semantics
in cross-module DSP code where stdlib imports use builtins (dsp/signal::db_to_linear
calls builtin log) while user code defines custom effects (Log effect operation).

Key changes:
- Parser: handle minus operator in parse_effect_refs() for subtraction syntax
- Checker: fn_declared_effects tracks which effects a function declares, used to
  disambiguate op vs builtin dispatch in should_dispatch_as_op()
- Examples: dsp_sandbox.lux demonstrates full DSP sandbox with effect subtraction
  and custom Log effect; effect_algebra.lux extended with subtraction comparison
- Docs: Phase 8B marked complete, Pain Point #1 resolved

All 21 examples pass. Clippy clean. Zero runtime cost — purely compile-time.

noodles/451880b:
The staff drew an inversion's slash bass at 36 + bass, C2 territory, and
nothing in the app ever sounds there: the sub plays 48 + bass on every
path - live playback, the comp attack, the chord editor's preview, the
circle's audition - anchored regardless of the harmony octave. Now the
slash engraves at that octave, exempt from the octave shift the rest of
the tower takes, deduped when the led triad's own bottom voice already
sits on the sub's pitch (a first inversion often does - one sounding
unison, one head). Every notehead on the plate is now a pitch the harmony
instrument plays that bar; the layers that stay un-notated (halo an
octave over the top voice, the sub doubling the root in root position)
are pure octave doublings of drawn tones, which is registration, which
charts have never notated.

Same pass: the roll staffs' key signatures drop to whisper opacity. Roll
noteheads are grid-aligned to the columns below, so a five-sharp
signature necessarily runs under the first steps - it always did, in text
glyphs too. Layered dim under the filled heads it reads as ambient
context, the same idiom the circle sheet already uses for its signature.
The plate keeps full-strength signatures; it owns its own left edge.

Verified: smoke green (one run hit the known press-drag flake, clean on
rerun); .tmp/pa-staff-receipts.mjs re-rendered - the G7/B tower seats its
B in the space above the bass staff's top line with a single head, and
the F-sharp-major roll reads clean over the whispered signature.
DESIGN-STAFF.md's grand-staff argument is restated from the sounding
registers instead of the retired C2 seat.
